I've never been able to understand what's the use of space exploration programs, its not like we are getting any closer to land on Mars than we were a few decades away.

Consider this: If all the budget on space programs in last two decades were used for economic growth and development instead, how much better we would have been economically! What exactly do we achieve from these space exploration programs?

The first nation that figures out how to exploit resources from elsewhere in the solar system is going to have a huge advantage. The fact that hunger exists is irrelevant to the need for scientific research.

This is a very short sighted view. Imagine you were living in the late 18th century and you were saying how all this research into steam machines and railroads is justified when people are going hungry. It was worth it in the end. Space is an absolute necessity for the survival of humanity. Once we start running out of resources we will need to resort to mining in space. If we perfect nuclear fusion we can harvest the necessary elements from the surface of the moon, thus creating essentially infinite energy. We can also offload millions of people from our overcrowded earth onto space colonies. It's an investment into the future, the only problem will be to ensure the space profits are shared fairly and equally, and not just reaped by a small elite. Research and development are extremely important, in fact I do believe we should spend much more on it.

Ever use GPS? Have you ever used satellite tv or radio? These things come from space research, among many others that I can't think of at the moment.

In my view the main benefit to humanity from space exploration is the pushing of the technology envelope. If we don't have difficult problems so solve, technology doesn't get created. When we put a man on the moon the trickle down of technology into civilian life was tremendous. Some Tech that is a direct spinoff of the space programs: Firefighter breathing apparatus, Carbon fiber, Better sunglasses (scratch resistant), Freeze-dried meals, Baby food (yes really, google it), Battery-powered thermal boots, The self-righting life raft, Satellite television, GPS, Water purification. These are just a few things, some seem silly. The list is endless, we really do get a lot back from space exploration.
Giving a poor person food feeds him for that day. Each day we explore space is a step forward for all of humanity.

In 5 billion years, our Sun will go supernova and destroy the Earth. Any human civilization (let alone life as we know it) on Earth will be lost.

We need to learn how to survive off-world. Not just in air-filled aluminum tubes, but to actually live without suits and masks on another world. Or, in the very least, find a way to recycle what we use/need to be self-sustaining in a sealed aluminum tube.

The world economy is currently polluting our world, and someday soon, it might not be very hospitable for people (or life in general). So the time to get to space and figure out our space-faring future is now.

Meanwhile, it's sad but true that there are just some human beings that will never contribute to that goal. Maybe they're born poor (wrong place, wrong time), maybe they are just stupid lazy fucks, but some people are just destined to be cannon fodder. You could dump millions of dollars into them and they still won't contribute anything meaningful to that goal, only slow it down.

I'm not saying that's right. That's just the unfairness of life.

Stupid view, we don't even put as much money as the US can into space programs. If the US gave a damn, or if some nation started militarizing then yes, the US would switch the space budget with the Military budget and start giving a damn.
